promises.promise: V.D. Satheesan pledged to develop a master plan to transform Kochi into a model city within six months.
V.D. Satheesan promised to resign from politics if the UDF does not win the upcoming Kerala elections.
The UDF is confident of winning over 100 seats in the upcoming Kerala elections.

recent_articles.title: CBI To Probe Death Of Ex-Kerala OfficialNaveen Babu, Daughter To Get Government Job
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Kerala** government has decided to hand over the investigation into the death of former Kannur Additional District Magistrate Naveen Babu to the **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)**. The decision follows family demands for a central agency inquiry and concerns about unanswered questions surrounding his death, which occurred on August 15, 2024.  The government also decided to provide a compassionate appointment to Naveen Babu's daughter, Niranjana.

recent_articles.title: Kerala faces burden of ₹5.07-lakh crore liabilities; fiscal structure under ‘serious’ strain, says White Paper tabled by CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan** tabled a white paper in the State Assembly on Thursday, June 4, 2026, highlighting Kerala's fiscal strain. The document states that the state faces a large burden of outstanding liabilities and high interest payments, while its capital expenditure is among the lowest in India despite a high fiscal deficit.  The white paper also points to "parallel governance structures" like the **Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB)** as contributing to the fiscal stress.

recent_articles.title: 36 arrests in a day as Kochi City police launch ‘Operation Toofan’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kochi City police** conducted a series of raids as part of the "Operation Toofan: The Narco Hunt" initiative, resulting in 33 NDPS Act cases and 36 arrests across 90 locations.  The largest seizure involved 437.28 grams of suspected MDMA found at Kollamkudi Mugal near Thrikkakara. **Assistant Commissioner of Police (Narcotics Cell) T.D. Sunilkumar** led the District Anti-Narcotics Special Action Force, which also includes teams from various police stations.  The operation was launched by Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan and overseen by **Inspector General (Intelligence) Putta Vimaladitya**, who serves as the State nodal officer for the project.

recent_articles.title: Why the furore over Rathan Kelkar’s appointment as secretary to Kerala CM Satheesan - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rathan Kelkar**, a former Kerala chief electoral officer, has been appointed secretary to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan by the new UDF government. **Kelkar** was previously praised for his integrity and efficiency during his tenure as chief electoral officer under the previous Left Front rule. The opposition CPI(M) and BJP have questioned this appointment, citing a similar case in West Bengal where the chief electoral officer was appointed as chief secretary. However, **Satheesan** defends the decision, emphasizing **Kelkar's** track record and due process.

recent_articles.title: Kerala CM directs withdrawal of suspension order of school Principal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, Kerala Chief Minister, ordered the reinstatement of a suspended **Javad S.**, Principal of Government Model Boys Higher Secondary School in Attingal. The suspension was based on an outside complaint and issued two days before the teacher's retirement.  The decision came after protests by government employees and teachers who argued that no preliminary investigation was conducted and that the government's stance against criticism was anti-democratic.

recent_articles.title: Mundamveli residents lay day-long siege to GCDA headquarters - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Residents of the P&T Apartment Complex in Mundamveli protested at the **Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA)** headquarters on Tuesday, demanding a probe into alleged violations of distance norms from an 110 kV EHT line. The residents, who moved into the twin towers built by the GCDA in January 2024, have been facing electrical problems and leakage issues since moving in. **Kochi MLA Mohammed Shiyas** visited the protest site and promised to petition the Chief Minister for a Vigilance probe.  The GCDA maintains that the apartments were constructed with all necessary permissions but acknowledged the need to address the residents' concerns about the safety of the structures.

recent_articles.title: UDF government will scrutinise steps taken by previous LDF government in MSC Elsa 3 disaster, says V.D. Satheesan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan** stated that the government would scrutinize the measures taken by the previous LDF government regarding the environmental damage caused by the MSC Elsa 3 shipping disaster and may amend the admiralty suit filed for compensation. The cabinet also approved a policy speech for the Governor in the Kerala Legislative Assembly on May 29th, appointed Apu John Joseph as Government Chief Whip, and K.C. Vincent as the new Additional Advocate General.  The government will convene a high-level meeting at 10 a.m. on Wednesday to prepare for the monsoon season.

recent_articles.title: ‘Needless fuss’: Kerala CM V.D. Satheesan defends posting former State poll chief Rathan Kelkar as his Secretary - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan** stated that the appointment of **Rathan U. Kelkar**, former Chief Electoral Officer (Kerala), as his Secretary was not a cause for concern and dismissed criticisms from the opposition.  He emphasized that no political party in Kerala had accused Mr. Kelkar of election manipulation, noting that he was appointed by the previous CPI(M)-led LDF government. **Mr. Satheesan** further highlighted that Mr. Kelkar's appointment is not comparable to similar controversies in West Bengal where allegations against the CEO were made.

recent_articles.title: Former Kerala Chief Electoral Officer Rathan U. Kelkar takes charge as Secretary to CM Satheesan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rathan U. Kelkar**, former Chief Electoral Officer of Kerala, assumed the role of Secretary to **Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan**.  The appointment has been met with criticism from the **CPI(M)** and **BJP**, who accuse the Congress of rewarding officials for election results. However, **Congress** leaders defend the decision, highlighting **Kelkar's** reputation as an efficient officer.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan offers Tulabharam at Guruvayur temple - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan** visited the **Guruvayur Sreekrishna Temple** on Sunday morning, offering prayers and performing the traditional Tulabharam ritual using 71 kg of butter. He was received by **devaswom chairperson A. V. Gopinath** and administrator **O. B. Arun Kumar**.  After the ceremony, **Satheesan** attended the wedding ceremony of **Revenue Minister A. P. Anilkumar’s** son.

recent_articles.title: Master plan to transform Kochi into model city to come up in six months, says Satheesan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan** announced a plan to transform **Kochi** into a model city with seamless transport and world-class infrastructure through a "twin city" expansion.  He emphasized the government's commitment to improving people's quality of life, boosting Kerala's economy, and addressing issues like brain drain.  The Chief Minister also pledged to distribute wealth fairly among all sections of society and prevent communalism. **Actor Mammootty** and **Actor Mohanlal** expressed their support for his vision.

recent_articles.title: KSRTC driver suspended over defamatory post against Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **KSRTC** driver S. Sunilkumar has been suspended for posting defamatory content about **Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan** on Facebook and circulating his picture in a defamatory manner. The corporation initiated disciplinary action against him, while the police are considering filing an IT Act case.  Further investigation is underway with the assistance of the cyber cell.

recent_articles.title: Chief Electoral Officer (Kerala) Rathan U. Kelkar appointed Secretary to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rathan U. Kelkar**, the Chief Electoral Officer of **Kerala**, will transition from his role to become the Secretary to **Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan**.  Mr. Kelkar, a 2003 batch IAS officer, has been in the news for overseeing the recent Kerala Assembly elections and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The appointment follows the recent appointment of **Manoj Kumar Agarwal** as Chief Secretary to the new BJP government in West Bengal.  The State government will send a panel of names to the Election Commission to appoint a new CEO once Mr. Kelkar is relieved of his duties.

recent_articles.title: Congress leader Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan elected Kerala Speaker - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan**, a senior Congress leader, was elected as the Speaker of the 16th Kerala Legislative Assembly on Friday (May 22, 2026). He won with 101 votes, defeating **A.C. Moideen** and **B.B. Gopakumar**.  The election took place after **G. Sudhakaran**, the previous Pro Tem Speaker, chose not to vote.  **V.D. Satheesan**, the Chief Minister, and **Pinarayi Vijayan**, the Leader of the Opposition, led Radhakrishnan to the Speaker's chair.

recent_articles.title: Full list of Kerala Cabinet Ministers by May 17, says Satheesan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, the newly appointed Chief Minister of Kerala, indicated that the full list of Ministers will be presented to **Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar** by Sunday evening.  The swearing-in ceremony is scheduled for Monday at 10 a.m., with speculation surrounding potential ministerial appointments within the **United Democratic Front (UDF)**. Senior Congress leader **Ramesh Chennithala**, reportedly disgruntled over not being chosen as Chief Minister, is rumored to be joining the Cabinet as Home Minister.  **K.C. Venugopal**, an aspirant for the CM's post, also met with Mr. Chennithala in conciliatory talks. The UDF is expected to finalize its ministerial appointments after discussions with all partners.

recent_articles.title: ASHAs meet Kerala CM-designate V.D. Satheesan, urge him to honour pre-poll promises - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala ASHA Health Workers’ Association (KAHWA)** met with **V.D. Satheesan**, the new Chief Minister-designate, to reiterate their demands for an increase in honorarium and retirement benefits. They expressed hope that the new government would prioritize addressing their concerns.  **Satheesan** assured them that he would not forget his pre-election promise of resolving their grievances.

recent_articles.title: Kerala politics LIVE: All eyes on Congress equations in Satheesan’s home turf ahead of Cabinet formation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, the newly designated Chief Minister-designate of the **United Democratic Front (UDF)**, has sparked speculation about potential Cabinet appointments in his stronghold of Ernakulam.  The UDF leadership met in Thiruvananthapuram on May 15th to discuss the new government's formation but did not make any final decisions regarding ministerial positions. The AICC general secretary **K.C. Venugopal** assured that differences among senior Congress leaders would be resolved amicably, paving the way for a smooth Cabinet selection process.

recent_articles.title: Watch: Congress ends suspense: V. D. Satheesan to be next Kerala CM | Above the Fold | 14.05.2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala Congress** named V.D. Satheesan as its new Chief Minister after weeks of internal discussions, ending months of uncertainty.  The **BRICS Foreign Ministers’ meeting**, hosted by India in New Delhi, saw **External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar** address key global challenges and diplomatic priorities.

recent_articles.title: Kerala’s Chief Minister-designate V.D. Satheesan holds out an olive branch to other contenders for the top post - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, the newly designated Chief Minister-designate for **Kerala**, expressed gratitude to **K.C. Venugopal** and **Ramesh Chennithala**, who were considered for the top post, while also acknowledging the contributions of other leaders within the **United Democratic Front (UDF)**.  He attributed the 10-day delay in selecting a Chief Minister to the "glut of choices" and emphasized that the final decision rests with the **Congress's high command**. He assured the people of **Kerala** of progress and development under his leadership, promising to work closely with the **UDF** to form the government.

recent_articles.title: Kerala CM announcement LIVE: Congress names V.D. Satheesan as Kerala CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **AICC** announced **V.D. Satheesan** as the Chief Minister designate of Kerala, ending a ten-day period of uncertainty following the May 4th election results. The announcement was made by **Ajay Maken**, **Mukul Wasnik**, and **Deepa Dasmunshi** at the AICC Office.  The Congress will now proceed to form the government in the state after securing the majority.

recent_articles.title: AICC begins consultations with Kerala leaders in New Delhi to decide on Congress’ CM candidate - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, **Sonia Gandhi**, and **Mallikarjun Kharge** met with top Kerala leaders in New Delhi on Tuesday to discuss the selection of a Chief Minister nominee for the state. The high command is seeking bipartisan support from former KPCC presidents, Congress MLAs-elect, and other key figures to restore organizational stability after the party's recent victory.  The meeting considered several potential candidates, including **K.C. Venugopal**, **V.D. Satheesan**, **Ramesh Chennithala**, and **Priyanka Gandhi Vadra**.  **K. Muraleedharan**, a KPCC insider, stated that the high command would consider popular opinion in addition to legislative party numbers when making their decision.

recent_articles.title: Tussle over CM lays bare fault lines in Congress - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Congress** has created a political crisis following its recent election victory in Kerala, causing division within the United Democratic Front (UDF) and embarrassing allies like the **IUML**. The party's central leadership is struggling to choose a chief ministerial candidate, leading to internal conflict and discontent among both senior leaders and ordinary workers.  The situation has been exacerbated by the party's decision to ask sitting MPs not to contest, further fueling speculation about its lack of vision and preparedness for post-election governance.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Government formation LIVE: Impasse over chief ministerial candidate in Congress - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leadership held marathon discussions in **New Delhi** with the three main contenders for Kerala's Chief Minister position, **K.C. Venugopal**, **Ramesh Chennithala**, and **V.D. Satheesan**, and **KPCC president Sunny Joseph**.  The consultations, attended by observers **Ajay Maken** and **Mukul Wasnik**, have failed to reach a decision on the selection of a new Chief Minister despite discussions lasting over three hours.

recent_articles.title: CM selection a democratic process: Chennithala - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ramesh Chennithala**, a senior Congress leader, criticized the BJP for its alleged delay in selecting a Chief Minister after the 2025 Delhi Assembly elections. He defended the **Congress**'s democratic process and emphasized that decisions are made through discussions within the party.  Chennithala stated that five days is not an unreasonable time frame for such a decision, especially considering the complexity of the selection process. The Congress leadership has been meeting with various leaders to arrive at a consensus on the next Chief Minister.

recent_articles.title: Kerala’s fiscal worries - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, the **Kerala** Opposition Leader, claims that the newly elected **UDF** government inherited a nearly empty treasury from the **LDF**.  The new government faces challenges in managing Kerala's finances, including high expenditures on salaries, pensions, and interest payments, limited tax revenue potential, and the impact of the 16th Finance Commission awards. The outgoing Finance Minister, **K.N. Balagopal**, disputes these claims, emphasizing that the state is in a better financial position than it was under the previous government.  The new government will need to address these challenges to fulfill its promises of development and social welfare programs.

recent_articles.title: Three-hour meeting fails to end impasse over Congress Chief Minister for Kerala - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Despite consultations between **Congress** president Mallikarjun Kharge, Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi, and AICC general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal, senior leaders Ramesh Chennithala and V.D. Satheesan, and KPCC president Sunny Joseph, a decision on naming a Chief Minister for **Kerala** remains stalled.  The high command has until May 23 to finalize the candidate after considering claims from each faction, including those of Congress MLA-designates and constituents of the United Democratic Front (UDF). The consultations were marked by intense posturing and competing claims, with party workers removing aggressive flex boards and appeals made to maintain decorum.

recent_articles.title: Kerala CM debate: Kharge to hold crucial talks with senior leaders today evening - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mallikarjun Kharge**, **AICC president**, will meet with key figures in the Kerala Congress leadership, including **K.C. Venugopal**, **V.D. Satheesan**, and **Ramesh Chennithala**, on Saturday (May 9, 2026) to discuss the selection of a new Chief Minister.  **Rahul Gandhi** is expected to meet with the Kerala leaders after a consensus emerges from the meeting chaired by **Kharge**.

recent_articles.title: Final decision on Kerala CM turns into political cliff-hanger as ball now in Congress High Command’s court - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Congress** party in Kerala is facing uncertainty regarding the selection of its Chief Minister, with three potential candidates – **V.D. Satheesan**, **K.C. Venugopal**, and **Ramesh Chennithala** – vying for the position.  The decision appears to be pending a final announcement from the **Congress High Command**, who are reportedly meeting with the contenders in Delhi on Saturday.

recent_articles.title: Kerala election results: Congress high command to pick Kerala CM; most UDF allies for Satheesan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Congress Legislative Party** in Kerala authorized the party high command to choose the next Chief Minister after a resolution was passed.  **AICC** observers, **Mukul Wasnik**, **Ajay Maken**, and **Deepa Dasmunsi**, met with all 63 legislators to gauge their preferences for the position. The three frontrunners in the race are former Leader of Opposition **V.D. Satheesan**, **K.C. Venugopal**, and **Ramesh Chennithala**.  **UDF** allies, including the **IUML**, have indicated support for **Satheesan**, while **KPCC** president **Sunny Joseph** has called for a decision based on public sentiment. The observers will present their findings to the high command, who is expected to make a final call soon.

recent_articles.title: Kerala polls: Congress-led UDF won not due to any individual’s efforts but as people were fed up, says NSS general secretary - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **G. Sukumaran Nair**, general secretary of the **Nair Service Society (NSS)**, stated that the Congress-led UDF's victory in the 2026 Kerala Assembly polls was due to public dissatisfaction with the government and not individual efforts by anyone, including **V.D. Satheesan**.  **Mr. Nair** attributed the Left's loss to internal issues within the party, not anti-incumbency sentiment. While acknowledging differences with **Satheesan**, he emphasized that these were not used against him during the election and asserted that the NSS did not dictate support for any candidate.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Sixth straight win for V.D. Satheesan in Paravur - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, the UDF candidate, has won the Paravur Assembly constituency for a sixth consecutive time in Kerala's elections.  He secured 78,658 votes, defeating **E.T. Taison** of the LDF who received 58,058 votes. **Valsala Prasannakumar**, former Congress chairperson, finished third with 20,377 votes. This victory follows Satheesan's win in 2021 against M.T. Nixon of the LDF.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: UDF win was made massive by anti-Left voting - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **United Democratic Front (UDF)**, led by the **Congress**, has returned to power in Kerala after a decade-long absence.  Following four bypoll victories and strong performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and December's local body polls, the alliance secured a majority in the State Assembly. The victory was attributed to cohesive teamwork within Team UDF, guarantees and assurances to voters, effective campaigning, and criticisms of the outgoing **Left Democratic Front** government's policies.

recent_articles.title: Opposing campaigns in Kerala map out the best- and worst-case scenarios for their respective alliances - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, **K.C. Venugopal**, and **Ramesh Chennithala** of the **Congress** are optimistic about a potential victory for their alliance in the upcoming Kerala Assembly elections, citing recent electoral successes and a perceived shift in voter sentiment towards the opposition. The **United Democratic Front (UDF)**, led by the **Indian Union Muslim League (IUML)**, is banking on its strong support base among minorities and backward classes to counter the ruling **Left Democratic Front (LDF)**.  **CPI(M)** leaders believe voters will continue to trust the LDF's record of governance and welfare programs. The **BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA)** aims to capitalize on voter dissatisfaction with both the UDF and LDF, positioning itself as a development alternative.

recent_articles.title: ​Primary league: On the Congress, UDF, 2026 Kerala Assembly elections - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leaders in Kerala have been caught off guard by the **IUML's** public endorsement of  **V.D. Satheesan** for Chief Minister, despite the party's internal agreements to let the legislature choose its leader. This move has sparked concerns about sectarian tensions and the IUML's maximalist demands within the UDF coalition, potentially jeopardizing the Front's social base. The **IUML**, however, is urged to respect established norms of Kerala's coalition politics, which involve a collective leadership decision by all partners.

recent_articles.title: UDF will probe “corruption” in the cancellation of DBFOO power supply contracts if it comes to power: V.D. Satheesan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, leader of the Opposition, called for a probe into alleged corruption behind the cancellation of long-term power supply contracts by the **Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission** and the **KSEB**. He argued that the decision to cancel these contracts led to unscheduled loadsheddings and increased power costs for the state.  The contracts had guaranteed power at ₹4.29 per unit, but the cancellation resulted in higher costs of ₹6 to ₹12 per unit, causing daily losses of ₹15 crore to ₹20 crore for the KSEB.

recent_articles.title: UDF allies air discontent over Cong. leadership hopefuls ‘lobbying’ for support ahead of Assembly poll results - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leadership hopefuls are facing discontent among **UDF** allies, particularly the **IUML**, who criticize premature speculation and lobbying for top positions. The **IUML** fears this behavior will erode public support and moral authority within the UDF.  **KPCC** leaders have denied any leadership disputes but their "cast iron pledge" seems to be wavering in light of these actions.  The situation is being closely watched by **Rahul Gandhi**, who is expected to make a decisive call on the matter.

recent_articles.title: Kerala fireworks unit blast: CM, Opposition leader express condolences - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan** directed the government to provide timely medical care to victims of a fireworks manufacturing unit fire and explosion in Thrissur, Kerala.  **Mr. Vijayan** expressed condolences for the deaths and stated that expert doctors from outside the state may be called upon if needed. The State Disaster Management department allocated ₹50 lakh to meet emergency needs following the accident.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Congress, CPI(M) question delay in poll data publication - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, leader of the Opposition in Kerala, and the **Communist Party of India (Marxist)** have requested an explanation from the **Election Commission of India** regarding the delay in releasing the complete election data for the April 9, 2026, Kerala Assembly elections.  The request was made to the Chief Election Commissioner of India.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Satheesan writes to CEO opposing move to suspend e-Office - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, leader of the Opposition, has written to **Ratan Kelkar**, the Chief Electoral Officer, expressing concerns over the IT department's decision to suspend the e-Office system at the Secretariat during the election Model Code of Conduct.  Satheesan argues that this move creates a possibility of misuse and weakens transparency, raising questions about the timing of the rollout. He urges the Election Commission to intervene and postpone the upgrade until after the elections.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: NDA candidate alleges deal between CM, Opposition leader in Dharmadam, Peravur - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **K. Ranjith**, the NDA candidate in Dharmadam, accused **Pinarayi Vijayan** and **V.D. Satheesan** of a deal during a media address in Kannur.  Ranjith claimed the electoral contest was between the Left Democratic Front and the NDA, with the United Democratic Front candidate's campaign being minimal. He demanded the Election Commission verify campaign spending for **Pinarayi Vijayan**'s Dharmadam campaign and stated the NDA would file a formal complaint regarding the expenses.

recent_articles.title: Kerala polls: Satheesan says ‘paid’ surveys don’t reflect public mood, calls BJP ‘a wolf in sheep’s clothing’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, Leader of the Opposition in Kerala, criticized recent opinion polls as "fabricated" and lacking credibility, claiming they are attempts to create an artificial perception of a close race between parties. He expressed confidence that the **Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF)** will secure over 100 seats and form the government.  **Suresh Gopi**, MP, was also cited as expressing concerns about the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) and its potential to weaken institutions. Satheesan further criticized Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan for alleged violence against opposition supporters and accused the BJP of targeting minority groups.

recent_articles.title: UDF began preparations for Mission 2026 a year ago; it will win in Kerala: Satheesan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, leader of the **United Democratic Front (UDF)**, believes the party will win the upcoming Kerala elections due to increased organizational preparedness and a groundswell of support from various social groups. He stated that he would resign from politics if the UDF does not achieve victory in the polls.  The UDF is confident of winning as they have successfully brought back 90% of the social groups who left the party, creating a broader political platform with diverse stakeholders. The CPI(M) is facing internal rebellion and losing its influence in Kerala, while the Congress has been working to improve its performance by addressing issues like price rise and gold pilferage at Sabarimala.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Pinarayi signals willingness to accept Satheesan’s challenge for a one-to-one debate on LDF governance - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan** responded to **Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan's** challenge for a debate on the ten years of **LDF** governance by posting a progress report card highlighting achievements such as the Vizhinjam port project and land title distribution.  **Satheesan** criticized these claims as election-era hyperbole, demanding a face-to-face debate at a time and place chosen by **Vijayan**.  He also listed various issues he would address in the debate, including the CPI(M)-BJP electoral deal, the LDF's relationship with the SDPI, and the cost of living crisis.

recent_articles.title: Kerala polls: On SDPI votes, CPI’s Binoy Viswam says party hasn’t explicitly rejected any and ‘all votes welcome’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Binoy Viswam**, Kerala State secretary of the **Communist Party of India (CPI)**, stated that the party welcomes all votes and has no ideological alignment with communal organizations.  He clarified that the CPI does not seek SDPI votes and maintains a stance based on development and secularism.  Viswam also rejected allegations of a CPI(M)-BJP deal, claiming the real understanding lies between the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** and the **Indian National Congress**. He criticized the Centre's FCRA amendment Bill as revealing the BJP's hostile stance towards minorities.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly elections 2026: Kerala became a ‘debt model’ under Left rule, says Tharoor - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Shashi Tharoor**, Congress leader, criticized the **Pinarayi Vijayan-led LDF government** in Kerala for transforming the state's development model into a "debt model," citing high debt levels and economic stagnation. He argued that the future generations would bear the burden of this unsustainable financial situation.  Tharoor also highlighted the alleged exodus of young people from the state due to lack of employment opportunities, calling for an investor-friendly environment under the United Democratic Front (UDF) administration.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: Pinarayi pandering to minority and majority communalism to gain a few votes, says Satheesan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, leader of the Opposition, criticized **Pinarayi Vijayan**, Chief Minister of Kerala, for shifting between appeasement of minority and majority communities to gain votes.  Satheesan accused **Vijayan** of felicitating communal speakers, claiming ties with the Jamaat-e-Islami despite denying them, and failing to take action against CPI(M) members in the Sabarimala gold case. He also questioned the lack of action taken against **Vijayan's** son regarding a summons from the Enforcement Directorate.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls: CPI(M) accuses Congress of aiding BJP’s past wins in Thrissur, Nemom - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **M V Govindan**, **CPI(M)** state secretary, accused the **Congress** of enabling the BJP's victories in Thrissur and Nemom.  He claimed that the decline in Congress votes in both constituencies led to the BJP's wins.  Govindan asserted that the Left party consistently opposes the RSS and the BJP while the Congress has engaged in discussions with Sangh Parivar leaders. He expressed confidence that a similar outcome would be seen in upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Satheesan accuses Pinarayi of being an RSS agent - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, leader of the Opposition, countered **Pinarayi Vijayan**, Chief Minister of Kerala, by posting old photographs of CPI(M) leaders alongside BJP figures to refute accusations of bowing to the RSS.  Satheesan argued that the CPI(M) has had clandestine ties with the RSS throughout history and accused Vijayan of being an RSS agent. He cited examples like the 1977 election victory, support for V.P. Singh in 1989, and alleged secret dealings with RSS leaders.

## UDF Races to Finalize Seat-Sharing Ahead of Kerala Polls

The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) is scrambling to finalize its seat allocation for the upcoming Kerala Assembly elections. The move comes after the Left Democratic Front (LDF) announced its candidates quickly following the election proclamation, prompting the opposition to accelerate their own candidate selection process.  Leaders from the UDF met with representatives of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), a key ally in the coalition, at Aluva Palace on Sunday. While no specific demands were mentioned by the IUML, discussions focused on seat distribution and potential swaps between parties. The meeting concluded with a promise to meet again on Monday to finalize remaining details.  The UDF is facing internal challenges as well, including former KPCC president K. Sudhakaran's desire to contest from Kannur, which has caused delays in finalizing candidate lists.

recent_articles.title: Four sitting MPs’ keenness to contest Assembly polls puts Congress in a spot in Kerala - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article:
## Kerala Congress Faces Candidate Conflict Ahead of Elections

A brewing conflict within the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) is threatening to derail the party's election strategy.  Four sitting MPs, including K. Sudhakaran and Adoor Prakash, have publicly declared their intention to contest in the upcoming Assembly elections, defying the central leadership's directive for sitting MPs to step aside. This has sparked a poster war and fueled speculation about the future of the party's campaign. While Rahul Gandhi reportedly summoned Sudhakaran to Delhi to discourage his candidacy, the issue remains unresolved as the party high command grapples with the conflicting demands from local leaders.  

The conflict extends beyond Sudhakaran, with several other candidates voicing their opposition to proposed candidates outside their constituencies or districts. This has led to resignations and protests, highlighting a growing disconnect between local leadership and the central decision-making process. The controversy underscores the challenges facing the Congress as it seeks to regain lost ground in Pathanamthitta district, where community representation is a key concern.
